answer: A cipher seals each admission, and a falcon audits it later. Every identity must be sealed in by two holders outside its own cluster, and one seal serves one identity, so n aliases need n separate sealers rather than one friendly crew. Each ledge holds a single berth per epoch, and the k-th seal an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A falcon re-asks a random sealer each epoch; an unconfirmed seal clears the berth and forfeits every bond on that ledge, so pooled evidence gains nothing.
